correctness.rationale: Universal incidence proof: any shattered support meets each line in at most three points; two lines cannot shatter six points. The private/disjoint line isolation lemma proves sufficiency for each permitted five-point type and detects q=3 obstruction. Pair-incidence double counts give n0 and B_q,T_q and all coefficients; q=2 and q=3 treated separately. Every direct trace for q=2,3,4 up through size six and q=5 through size five agrees; q=5 size-six is sampled only. Proof covers all orders, including non-Desarguesian, without computational extrapolation.

evidence: Prior 2025 result proves that in the real plane a five-point set is shattered iff two lines cover it and no four points are collinear, together with exactly two incidence types.
For q=3, 468 one-triple sets satisfy those same incidence conditions yet fail to be shattered; 702 two-triple sets succeed. This is an explicit failed implication of the naïve finite transfer.
The current all-order coefficients and the sharp q=3/4 type distinction are not statements of the 2025 paper.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The upper bound and types are already subsumed at the level of geometric necessary incidence. It is neither identical to nor a mere restriction of the infinite-real-plane theorem; the finite projective hypothesis changes which traces exist.

originality.rationale: Real-plane five-point types and bound five are previously known from arxiv:2501.09847 and excluded from new contribution. The full finite-projective-plane coefficientwise polynomial and sharp q=3 loss of one incidence type are not implied by simply restricting its real-line statements. published-finding corpus and own-ledger claim comparisons found no equivalent finite-plane census. residual_risks: The 2025 real-line theorem is a very close structural predecessor; some q>=4 cases can be adapted from its proof with extra incidence counting. The novel claim must remain the finite-profile and q=3 correction, not the abstract types.
